transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hello, Dr. [Name]. I, um... I came in because I keep hearing these voices. It's like... clear as day, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio apartment. They keep saying my name, over and over, and telling me my work is being judged. And the thing is, the house is completely quiet. There's nobody there. It's just me and my plants. I have this beautiful pothos plant, you know, the ones with the heart-shaped leaves? I've had it for years, since I started working as an aide. It just keeps growing and growing, trailing all over the window. I water it every Sunday, regular as clockwork. But yeah, the voices... they just start up even when I'm just sitting there looking at my plant.
How long have you been hearing these voices saying your name and judging your work — days, weeks, or longer?

Well, it's been... let's see. About nine months now. Nine whole months of hearing them and having this awful, fixed fear that my work is being watched all the time. It started right around the time I bought my new vacuum cleaner. It’s one of those bagless ones, bright red. I needed a good one because I help some of my older clients keep their places tidy, you know, being an aide and all. And the old vacuum I had just wasn't picking up the dust anymore. Dust is so bad for the lungs, especially for the elderly folks. My uncle had terrible lungs, though he worked in a factory down in Ohio for years. He used to cough so loud it would wake the dog. He had a golden retriever named Buster. Such a sweet boy, Buster was. He loved to chew on old shoes, wouldn't even touch his actual toys. But yeah, that red vacuum has this little attachment for the corners that is just perfect for getting around the baseboards... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. Nine months. About nine months of the voices.

Over these past nine months, have you had any stretches of time—separate from the voices—where you felt persistently very sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things, or on the other hand, unusually elated, energetic, or needing very little sleep?

Well, yes, actually. Sometimes I get this... this feeling like I'm just so bright and chosen, you know? Like I have all these grand plans and Greenville is just too small to hold them all. I start thinking about starting my own agency, maybe hiring a whole fleet of aides. We'd all wear matching scrubs, maybe a nice calming blue. Blue is such a soothing color, don't you think? Like the ocean. I went to the beach once, years ago, down in Florida. The sand was so white it hurt your eyes, and the seagulls... oh, they would just swoop down and steal your french fries right out of your hand! I had this little paper boat of fries, perfectly salted, and swoosh! Gone. But anyway, yeah, I get so full of energy and ideas, but then... then it can just flip. Like, I'll be flying high, and then I'll just snap. Hard. Just the other day, one of my clients—sweet older lady, but she's hard of hearing—she asked me to repeat myself about what time her daughter was coming, and I just bit her head off. I felt terrible after, but in the moment, it just boiled up so fast. So, yes, I get those really high, energetic times, and then I get so irritable I can barely stand myself.
During the times when you're not feeling unusually high-energy or irritable—when your mood feels more normal or even—do you still hear those voices saying your name and judging your work?

Well, yes... yes, I do. Like, there was this one time recently after all that energy finally dropped off and I was actually sleeping a normal amount again. My mood felt pretty level, you know? But the voices... they just kept right on going for weeks. Telling me my work was being tracked and judged. It was so distracting, especially when I was trying to make my grocery list. I always write my lists on these little yellow legal pads. I like the yellow paper, it's easier on the eyes than stark white. And I use this special pen, a blue gel pen that glides so smoothly. I get them in a pack of five from the pharmacy down the street. The pharmacist there, Mr. Henderson, he's always so polite. He wears these little bow ties, different one every day. Last Tuesday it was polka dots. Red with white dots. Reminded me of Minnie Mouse. I always loved Minnie Mouse when I was a little girl, had a lunchbox with her on it and everything... but yes, even when my mood was completely fine and normal for those few weeks, the voices and that awful feeling of being watched were still there.

Over these full nine months, would you say the high-energy/irritable periods have been present most of the time, or have they been more brief episodes compared to the weeks or months when your mood felt normal?

Well, if I really think about the whole nine months... I'd say for most of that stretch, I was just completely wound up. You know, having all those big plans, getting barely any sleep, just nonstop activity day and night. Or if I wasn't flying quite that high, I was coming down from it but still just not back to my normal self. So yeah, most of the time it was like that. 

I remember one of those nights I couldn't sleep, it must have been 3 in the morning, and I was watching this infomercial for a food dehydrator. They were making apple chips and beef jerky right there on the TV. It looked so easy! My brother, Tommy, he used to make his own jerky in the garage. He had this big smoker out back. Smelled like hickory wood all summer long. We'd sit out there on lawn chairs and swat mosquitoes. The mosquitoes back home are just enormous, I swear they're the size of hummingbirds. You need that heavy-duty bug spray, the kind with DEET in it, even though it smells awful and leaves your skin all sticky and gross. I bought a two-pack of it at the hardware store when they had a clearance sale on summer items... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh. Right. But yes, most of the nine months I was either all revved up and not sleeping, or just feeling out of sorts from it.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications/supplements around the time these mood swings and voices started?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I don't drink or anything like that. Never had much of a taste for alcohol, honestly. My father, he used to drink this awful cheap beer, the kind that comes in those big aluminum cans. He'd leave them all over the porch, and the stray cats would come around and knock them over in the middle of the night. Clang, clang, clang! It would wake me up out of a dead sleep. We had this one stray, a big orange tabby with a torn ear. I called him Marmalade. He was the sweetest thing, but he loved to dig in the trash. I tried to feed him some canned tuna once, the chunk light kind in water, not oil—oil is too rich for their little stomachs, you know. I read that in a magazine at the dentist's office. The dentist, Dr. Shapiro, he always has the most outdated magazines. I think I read an article about Princess Diana in there just last month! But anyway, no, no drugs or new pills or anything like that. Just my regular vitamins, though I keep forgetting to take the calcium ones because they're so big. They look like horse pills! I tried breaking them in half, but they just crumble everywhere...

Concurrently, she describes manic-type symptoms (grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, irritability) that have been present for the majority of the illness duration. Critically, she confirms that during a period of weeks when her mood was completely normal (euthymic), the psychotic symptoms (voices, feeling watched) persisted unabated, establishing that psychotic symptoms occur independently of mood episodes for a significant period. No substance use or medical explanation identified. This combination—mood episode present for majority of active illness period plus psychotic symptoms persisting ≥2 weeks in absence of mood episode—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features (F30.2) or Schizophrenia (F20.9), which would require psychotic symptoms to dominate without mood congruence or reversed timing.
